findings: The exact client contains distinct asynchronous getter and setter symbols for both CPU Power Limit and Curve Optimizer.

Enable/disable is a separate discovered feature surface: server symbols name EnableCPUVoltageOptimizer and ResetVoltageOffset, while the captured client getter represents disabled optimizer state as zero.

The client exposes DeviceInit/DeviceTerminate plus RegisterFFIEvent/UnRegisterFFIEvent and server-state/close symbols; this supports an explicit client-ownership experiment rather than treating the generic service process as sufficient.
No StartAPPServer client symbol was found in the inspected symbol set. A restart-related lifecycle string exists, but its semantics and authorization requirements are not inferred.

nextSafeExperiment.name: PreconnectThenIsolate
steps: Verify the exact signed and hashed backend components.
Connect and register an OpenBlade client while Synapse still owns a live backend, without issuing a getter or setter.
Stop only preverified Synapse controller process IDs while keeping the OpenBlade client registered.
Recheck that Synapse is inactive, then issue getter-only requests.
Unregister and terminate the OpenBlade client, and restore Synapse from a finally path.
nextSafeExperiment.successBoundary: The getter must return exact in-policy values after Synapse exits while the OpenBlade client remains registered.
nextSafeExperiment.setterBoundary: Even a successful keep-alive getter does not admit setters; setter validation still requires save, set, independent readback, unconditional restore, and readback of the restored state.
